items.title: 61426_Jacques Butler oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee describes Pastotis as a 'great friend' of Billy Burns and details events involving Pastotis and Burns, but does not state a direct personal relationship with Pastotis himself.

ctx.x: Billy Burns was a caucasian man, but Billy Burns had a pair of lips on him that looked like steak lips, and he didn't care nothing about what he looked like. He was sort of man, he knowed what he looked like. He didn't want to hear it, he wanted to be a black man. / So, we left Billy Burns alone. Billy Burns had some rich woman, I think she was something -- the fiancee of the Minister of Finance of Belgium and Billy Burns would give parties and you would go in -- the bathtub would be full of Channel's Crepe de…

and that's the way Billy Burns lived. He could afford all of these hotel bills of $35.00 a day. All right, then, Burns and he was doing his various things, had certain drugs and whatever they had, their pleasures. Arabian delights and he and Pastotis were great friends and it seems as though Pastotis' wife, seemed to like Burns very much.

Then Pastotis' wife was -- Pastotis had an old car, I think it was an old Ford or something and Burns sent and got a Packard, beautiful Packard. This is around 1936 and the Packard was a beautiful thing. Then Burns took the Packard off the boat and Pastotis got that devil look in him and then the lady got that love look on her for Burns.
